step_by_step_reasoning: The whiteboard architecture depicts Amazie.io's Lagoon open-source application delivery platform. Developers push code to Git repositories, triggering webhooks to the Lagoon control plane hosted on Amazon EKS. Lagoon then deploys application environments onto target hosting EKS clusters. The target EKS cluster manages worker node groups running on EC2 (for persistent base workloads) and EC2 Spot instances (for non-production workloads, delivering 70-90% cost savings). Workloads interact with Amazon Aurora (running on Graviton2 R6g instances), EBS GP3 volumes (for database and search workloads like OpenSearch/Solr), and EFS (for general file storage). All nodes and directional connections are mapped faithfully based on visual and transcript evidence.
